To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sleep deprivation impairs memory consolidation in both rodents and humans, and that the molecular, cellular, circuit, and whole-brain mechanisms of this impairment are beginning to emerge.
Sleep deprivation alters molecular signaling pathways that are involved in memory processing and bidirectionally alters synaptic potentiation.
Sleep deprivation impairs synaptic plasticity and accelerates the loss of long-lasting forms synaptic plasticity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how sleep and sleep loss affect the brain's ability to encode, store, and recall information.
how sleep and sleep deprivation affect the brain’s ability to learn and remember.
the role of sleep and sleep loss on the brain and behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sleep is necessary for memory consolidation.
sleep is a fundamental requirement for memory formation and consolidation.
sleep is essential to the consolidation of memory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the unique neurophysiology of sleep exerts profound effects on molecular, celluar, and network mechanisms of synaptic plasticity, which in turn regulate both initial memory encoding and subsequent long-term consolidation.

the sleep-dependent consolidation of memory is an emergent property of the brain, and that it results from a dynamic interplay between sleep and the molecular, cellular and whole-brain networks that underlie plasticity and memory.
sleep is a critical component of memory processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sleep, in addition to its many other functions, may be critical for maintaining the brain in a state of readiness for new learning and the consolidation of recent memories.
sleep and plasticity are intimately linked and that the same molecular and network processes that underlie memory encoding and consolidation also regulate sleep.
the sleep-dependent consolidation process is a fundamental component of memory processing, and that sleep is a powerful tool to manipulate the brain’s capacity for learning.
